items.text: Task from the agent that started it: stored encrypted.

items.html:
Recommend one fresh worker per tree and case, sequentially, preserving current ABBA ordering. This is the smallest portable isolation fix.

  • run_round() currently measures each case only once per worker. The persistent functions cache therefore provides no reuse of a case’s prepared inputs across requests.
  • time_call() already evaluates the function before timed samples; round zero also evaluates it for value agreement. Fresh processes retain these warmed samples.
  • Keep existing Worker, but construct, measure, and close it inside each (name, label) iteration, with finally or a narrow ExitStack. No simultaneous comparison workers remain.
  • The cost is repeated imports, particularly the 33 framework cases each round, and losing cross-case import/cache state. Imports remain outside measured time. Comparisons become more self-contained, though complete suite wall time increases.

SIGSTOP/SIGCONT needs more than a change inside measure():

  1. Both workers currently begin importing before the first measurement. Pause-after-measure leaves startup competition intact.
  2. Sending SIGSTOP does not acknowledge that the worker’s threads have stopped. Confirm the stopped state before starting its peer, or a race remains.
  3. Returning the JSON line and self-stopping afterward also races: the parent can resume it before it stops, leaving the next request blocked.
  4. Existing close() sends SIGTERM and waits. A stopped worker must first receive SIGCONT, or be killed directly, before waiting; otherwise failure cleanup can hang.
  5. Waiting on process state must preserve Popen exit/reaping ownership. This adds lifecycle complexity and excludes Windows without another execution path.

OpenBLAS timeout/wait settings are a useful diagnostic or explicitly documented configuration, but backend-specific tuning does not establish isolation from other BLAS, OpenMP, JAX, or Rayon pools.

Existing tests cover failed-worker cleanup, protocol stdout purity, alternating order, and identical-tree agreement. For sequential workers, adjust the cleanup test’s assumption that both workers were started, and verify that the first worker is reaped before the next is created. A signal solution additionally needs successful suspension/resumption and cleanup of a stopped peer after failure.

Read-only review; no edits, timing, or tests run.
